answer: Each identity claims one onyx block in a yarrow bay, locks a 70-credit bond, and files serial, dimensions, and weight from the zenith hoist scale. An auditor re-measures the block, recomputes weight from the onyx density table, and burns the bond if filed weight differs by over 2% or one serial appears in two bays. First costs 31; the k-th costs 31+9(k-1), so the 1000th costs 9022 and 1000 fakes pay 4,526,500 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-block ring fails: a rented block sits in the wrong yarrow bay or repeats its serial. An honest claimant pays 31 once and recovers the bond after audit.
